test_title: PYST 41 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Transform the above assertive sentence into an interrogative sentence.

"Electronic devices have become indispensable to modern life."

options.text: Why electronic devices have become indispensable to modern life?
Had electronic devices have become indispensable to modern life?
Are electronic devices become indispensable to modern life?
Have electronic devices become indispensable to modern life?

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: Have electronic devices become indispensable to modern life?***

 
 
• To transform an **assertive** sentence into an **interrogative** (Yes/No) sentence, we move the auxiliary verb to the beginning of the sentence, before the subject.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Present Perfect Tense** ("have become"). Therefore, we move the auxiliary **"Have"** to the front: *Have + Subject (electronic devices) + Verb (become)...?*
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Why electronic devices have become...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While it is a question, it lacks the necessary subject-auxiliary inversion. A correct "wh-" question would be: "Why **have** electronic devices become...?"
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Had electronic devices have become...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. It incorrectly changes the tense to Past Perfect ("Had") and includes a redundant auxiliary "have."
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Are electronic devices become...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The auxiliary "are" belongs to the continuous or passive voice, but the main verb "become" requires the auxiliary "have" for the perfect tense used in this context.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rule for Transformation**: If the assertive sentence has an auxiliary verb (is, are, have, has, will, can), simply swap the position of the subject and the auxiliary.
 
• **Adding "Do/Does/Did"**: If the assertive sentence has no auxiliary verb (e.g., "They recycle e-waste"), use a form of "do" to create the question (e.g., "**Do** they recycle e-waste?").
 
• **Punctuation**: Always remember to replace the full stop (.) with a question mark (?) at the end of the sentence.
